full_judgment:
From a reading of the provisions of the aforesaid Rule we are of the view that the carrier is prima facie liable for loss of goods if the loss took place during the carriage, and that the period of carriage comprises the period during which the goods are in charge of the carrier. The delivery of the consignments in the instant case to the defendant No. 1, the agent of the carrier, is no delivery to the consignee. Hence both the carrier and their agent are liable for the loss of the cartons as baileys. It has been argued by the learned Advocate for the defendant No. 1 that since their principal, the defendant No. 2 has not made any allegations of negligence and misconduct they cannot be held liable for loss of the cartons. D.W. 2 on behalf of defendant No. 2 has deposed that the consignments were made over by the defendant No. 1 to the customs. We have held that the cartons were lost while those were in custody of the defendant No. 1. In view of the loss of the cartons initial liability for the loss lies upon the carrier and its agent and a presumption of negligence has arisen therefor. Nothing has been shown by defendant Nos. 1 and 2 to rebut the presumptions. On the contrary, defendant Nos. 1 and 2 have pleaded that the consignments were in custody of the customs or rather they disowned its custody. Hence there is ho scope of pleading that the carrier or its agent took all precautions to protect the consignments as a prudent man until its delivery to the consignee. 

 15. With regard to the objection as to the defect in the notice sent by the plaintiff before filing of the suit, it appears to us that provisions under section 26 of Carriage by Air (International Convention) Act IX of 1966 do not apply to loss of cargo and short delivery of the same by the carrier or his agent to the consignee. Rule 26 lays down that in case of damage of goods complaint to they carrier for recovery of such damage must be made normally with. 14 days from the date of receipt of the goods and in case of delay of delivery of the goods the complaint is to be made within 21 days from the date on which the goods were placed at the disposal of the consignee. From a reading of the provisions of Rules 18,22 and 26 we are of the view that words 'loss' and 'damage' have been distinctly used and meant in the aforesaid Act to convey different meanings. The meaning of the word damage in Rule 26 distinguished from the word 'loss' used in Rules 18 and 22 would mean harm or injury to goods as such and not damage by loss of goods. This interpretation appears to be harmonious and compatibles with the other relevant provisions of the Act. Conceding that the provisions of Rule 26 are applicable, it also appears that notice of loss of cartons having been made within 21 days, the suit cannot be held to be bad on account of defect in the notices (Exts. 1 and 1 (ka)) of complaint of such loss. We, therefore, find no substance in the contentions of the learned Advocate for the appellant on this ground. On the question of the liability of the defendant No. 1 as agent of defendant No. 2 Mr. Nurul Alain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant No. 1 appellant has submitted that the principal having been impleaded in the suit the agent cannot be held liable for the alleged loss of the cartons. In the facts and circumstances of the cases it has been found that the consignments were in custody of defendant No. 1, the agent of defendant No. 2. Once the custody of the consignments have been proved to the with the defendant No. 1 the carrier as well as their agent are liable for loss of the cartons since the carrier and its agent has failed to displace the presumptions of negligence and to prove how the consignments were dealt with after their landing at Dacca Airport. We have already observed that Rule 18 has created an initial statutory liability for loss of, the consignments from the Airport which could be rebutted by them. In our considered view there is no escape from the conclusion that the defendant Nos. 2 and 1 are both responsible as carrier and its agent respectively for loss of the cartons and the learned Subordinate Judge rightly decreed the suits against them. The decisions refer-red to by the learned Advocate for the defendant No. 1, reported in 19 D.L.R. page 75 and 21 D.L.R. (S.C.). 245 are not applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case.
